This is the one-day workshop on the EU-frames case, which works on a study of Eurobarometer surveys: its original author (OA) asked whether the economic crisis changed how citizens of the member states frame the European Union, and five analysts reanalysed one claim of the study in the Multi100 project. Across the day you work as analyst no. 6, in four parts: the claim and the credibility of social science, the estimand and the causal graph, the reproduction of a recorded result, and robustness, with the specification menu, the class chart, the curve of 864 specifications of the claim and one analysis declared before it runs.

You leave with an estimand and a causal graph of your own, a reproduced result, two dots on the class chart, one explored and one declared, and the place of your result on the curve of 864.

## How you work

The day is taught mainly in the browser lab, a page of the course site on which R runs inside your browser, with nothing to install. It works on aggregate data only, the country-year panel of the course and two files that the course rebuilt for two of the analysts, all three held by the lab; the respondents themselves are a subject of the third day of the Extended course. The workspace that you install before the day, in your IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), holds the same tasks and gives the same numbers.

[Open the browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Install R and the workspace](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

Several of the steps are things that the class does together, such as everyone typing the value that they have just reproduced and holding it back until the facilitator says go, so the day needs a facilitator. Some stretches of the slides are optional, the tutorial on the methods behind the menu and the background of the multiverse in the last part, and the facilitator switches them on or off to suit the class. The day runs in four parts, with a break after the first and the third and lunch after the second.

## The parts of the day

- **[Before the day](before.qmd).** You install R and the workspace, work through the first module on R, and read the case study.
- **[Part 1 – The claim and credibility](part-1.qmd).** The part sets out the credibility debate, what 'replication' names, Multi100 from the inside and the paper with its record in SCORE, and it ends with R running on your machine.
- **[Part 2 – The estimand and the causal graph](part-2.qmd).** You meet estimands and a short course on causal graphs, and then you write the estimand and finish the graph.
- **[Part 3 – The reproduction](part-3.qmd).** You reproduce the result of C6HJR, KQXUE or 018OL, read the three models side by side, meet the problem of few clusters, and read the code that your analyst deposited.
- **[Part 4 – Robustness](part-4.qmd).** You work the menu and put an exploratory dot on the class chart, read the chart against the curve of 864, ask what the curve establishes and what a replication would have to fix, and declare one analysis before it runs.
- **[After the day](after.qmd).** The page says where to go next in the companion curriculum.

[Start with Before the day](before.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

The same case is also taught as a [short session](../eu-frames-short/index.qmd) of three hours, as the [Extended course](../eu-frames-extended/index.qmd), whose second day is this workshop, and as a [self-study route](../self-study/index.qmd).
